steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: Wow, this is way more dangerous than your experiments at Rhodes Island.

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: You used to blow up your lab like three or four times a day, at most. Now, you're doing it once every fifteen minutes.

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: That's not the kind of data I want...

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: Don't worry, I made detailed records of all your experiments so far. Clean the desk up, won't you, Peludita?

steps.name: Pascuala
steps.text: Sure thing!

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: What is she doing here?

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: I felt like I could use an assistant myself. Don't worry, she's clever and hardworking enough.

steps.name: Pascuala
steps.text: (And you're making me do all your work!)

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: Ahem. How about you go fetch some fin oil and Oriron from the warehouse?

steps.name: Pascuala
steps.text: On it!

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: Alright, she's gone...

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: Now, what's the problem we're dealing with?

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: We're not making much progress... The samples that I've managed to construct are well below the required standard.

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: Really? They look good though. Nice and shiny.

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: There's a reason Corazonix is so rare. Its incredible powers are supported by an extraordinarily complex structure.

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: Either I'm not doing this right, or my understanding of Corazonix is completely wrong.

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: I'm not ready to manipulate true Corazonix, not even close.

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: So why not make more samples until you're satisfied with them?

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: Our resources are limited, I can't use them all... If I fail, I at least want to leave some behind for them.

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: You've barely started and you're already thinking about your inevitable failure. Come on, have some faith in yourself.

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: We've worked together so many times. I have faith in you. So does Señora Juana, and, er... er...

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: ...Who else was there again?

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: Well, that certain someone, at least...

steps.name: Pascuala
steps.text: And me.

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: Oh, hey there, Peludita. You're back already?

steps.name: Pascuala
steps.text: I, for one, am rooting for your success.

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: What's in it for you, Pascuala?

steps.name: Pascuala
steps.text: Don't forget I was the one who brought this compass here. If you screw this up, I'm screwed too.

steps.name: Pascuala
steps.text: So, don't send me away again when you run into trouble. I'll do what I can to help.

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: ...Well, to start with, you could help by not selling me out this time.

steps.name: Pascuala
steps.text: Tch, believe what you want...

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: Ahem. Anyway, thanks for running that errand. I'm going to adjust the direction of the transmutation table. Could you sort out the ingredients?

steps.name: Pascuala
steps.text: Fine, fine.

steps.name: Pascuala
steps.text: (All you do is nag!)

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: Come in!

steps.name: Teach
steps.text: Sorry to interrupt. There's something I want to ask.

steps.name: Teach
steps.text: The transmission core on one of the salt ships just broke, and we couldn't find any material strong enough... I get that the boss gave you those materials for the compass, but we just need a little...

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: How much?

steps.name: Teach
steps.text: One hundred grams.

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: Pascuala will fetch it.

steps.name: Pascuala
steps.text: (Whisper) Are you kidding me? That's everything we've got!

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: Go.

steps.name: Pascuala
steps.text: But...

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: Just go. We don't need it for the experiments just yet.

steps.name: Teach
steps.text: Muchas gracias. Sorry for asking at a time like this. Señora Juana said the compass takes priority over everything else...

steps.name: Teach
steps.text: The future of the whole fleet is on you.

steps.name: Teach
steps.text: Isidro?

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: Please don't say that.

steps.name: Teach
steps.text: ...Is it not going well?

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: Don't you worry, señora. It's only been a few days! He's feeling stressed, that's all.

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: If you ask me, it's a good thing! Nothing like a little pressure to keep you sharp.

steps.name: Teach
steps.text: Word of advice, Isidro. Whatever happens in the lab, good or bad, don't tell a soul.

steps.name: Teach
steps.text: Resentment towards Juana has been growing for years due to her radical decisions. Many are watching closely, waiting for the slightest slip-up.

steps.name: Teach
steps.text: Waiting for their chance to take the leadership from her.

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: I didn't realize there would be so many complications when I agreed to repair the compass.

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: What about you, Señora Teach?

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: Are you one of the people watching?

steps.name: Teach
steps.text: Of course I'm watching you, chaval. But I don't give a sandfin's ass about the compass, I only care about Juana.

steps.name: Teach
steps.text: If you fail, it's up to me to keep her safe, and...

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: And what?

steps.name: Teach
steps.text: And keep you all from being torn to pieces by a horde of angry pirates.

steps.name: Teach
steps.text: This is a pirate ship, and don't you forget that.

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: Thorns...
Isidro does not answer. His expression is grave, and the shadows on his face hang like heavy curtains in the night.
Several pirates are still working under the dim lamplight. They look up at the pair with probing gazes as they walk by.
Isidro has never felt so intently that his every move is being watched.

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: If you're starting to have second thoughts, I've got your back.

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: (Whisper) I'm sure the two of us could slip out by ourselves, no problem.

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: ...Sorry to drag you into this, Elysium.

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: Oh, spare me, I chose to come here.

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: I just wanted to help them find a way out. Maybe satisfy my own desires along the way...

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: But things are far more complicated than I thought. Far too many people have placed their hopes in me, in this compass.

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: Some of those hopes are even contradictory. Some want me to succeed, some want me to fail, others want me to do nothing at all.

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: I don't like it.

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: I feel you, amigo.

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: But that's how people are. Anything you do is inevitably going to affect someone else. Not saying you need to feel responsible, but it couldn't hurt to give it some thought.

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: The whole thing makes my head hurt... I'd much rather be working alone.

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: You haven't been alone for a long time now, buddy.

steps.name: Juana
steps.text: You really gave Teach all the sinew?

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: ...Did Pascuala tell you?

steps.name: Juana
steps.text: Oh, you needn't worry about that. I certainly didn't order her to show up at your lab.

steps.name: Juana
steps.text: I realize you'd rather not be bothered. I just felt compelled to check on your progress.

steps.name: Juana
steps.text: Do you need more sinew?

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: Unless my eyes deceived me, that wasn't saltfin sinew... That was taken from Seaborn.

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: But I thought you wiped out the Seaborn on the Salt Flat.

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: Wait... are you going to kill it? But...

steps.name: Juana
steps.text: ...Come with me.

steps.name: Juana
steps.text: Cruz would have done the same.

steps.name: Rus
steps.text: I told you Juana wouldn't listen.

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: I know...

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: I did it to keep her from learning about your conversation with the shipwrights. She was going to talk to them yesterday.

steps.name: Rus
steps.text: We simply talked about work. What's there to hide?

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: Teach may not have realized, but I have. It doesn't take that much sinew to fix a transmission core.

steps.name: Rus
steps.text: ...So you knew all along?

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: What are your next plans?

steps.name: Rus
steps.text: The compass repairs will grind to a halt without enough materials.

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: Juana won't stop just because of a little material shortage. She'll go get more with the kid.

steps.name: Rus
steps.text: I heard it was taken from the sea monsters Captain Cruz killed... but there aren't any sea monsters around anymore.

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: No, there are... I've seen it.

steps.name: Rus
steps.text: So... the rumors were true?

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: Doesn't matter anymore. What matters is what we can do while she's gone.

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: Hey, Peludita, have you seen Thorns?

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: Did he head to the lab already? At this hour?

steps.name: Pascuala
steps.text: *yawn*

steps.name: Pascuala
steps.text: No clue. He didn't come back last night.

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: You waited all night for him?

steps.name: Pascuala
steps.text: Not me, Nene. It laid down at the door and didn't budge all night.

steps.name: Nene
steps.text: (Shakes tail anxiously)

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: That's odd. I'll check out the lab. Go get some sleep.

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: Can't work without sleep. No point trying to play it tough; I'll wake you up if there's anything.

steps.name: Pascuala
steps.text: Did he really think I could fall asleep at a time like this? That guy's loco.

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: Um, excuse me? Are you looking for someone?

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: Is Pascuala here?
The sound of clashing swords echoes through the cave. Isidro slices a sharp arc in the air, cutting cleanly through the Seaborn's flesh.
Yet, the creature is relentless, its appendages flailing wildly. Blades embedded within its limbs streak across the air like shooting stars.
A fencer's rapier, a bladecaster's sword-wand, a knight's great sword, an assassin's dagger, a samurai's katana... one after another, they rush towards Isidro, threatening to overwhelm his vision.
Finally, there is a pirate's cutlass, screaming as it cuts through the air, as if battling the wind and waves, like in the legends.

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: Hmph...

steps.name: Sword-wielding Seaborn
steps.text: Gugh...

steps.name: Juana
steps.text: I used to ask myself every day... why wasn't I the one who was devoured?

steps.name: Juana
steps.text: This was your burden to bear... so why leave it to me?

steps.name: Juana
steps.text: You were the one who should have sat in the captain's chair, and I should have been your helmswoman, drenched from head to toe by the ocean's spray.

steps.name: Juana
steps.text: Oh, how I've loathed you for this, Cruz.
The night wind of the Salt Flat carries the familiar smell of brine.
A single tear falls from the corner of Juana's eye, scattered by the wind before it hits the ground.

steps.name: Juana
steps.text: Your swordplay has already improved tremendously. I thought it would take more time.

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: I'm sorry...

steps.name: Juana
steps.text: For what? I'd have joined you in that cave, if I weren't recovering from my injuries.

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: ...Were you crying?

steps.name: Juana
steps.text: What did I tell you about asking a lady a question she'd rather not answer?

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: ...My apologies.

steps.name: Juana
steps.text: There's no need to feel bad. I was planning to ask you to kill hi—it eventually, once you were strong enough.

steps.name: Juana
steps.text: We just moved up the schedule. You must be incredibly talented with a blade to have accomplished it so soon.

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: It... had a sword with the name Cruz on it.

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: I thought you should have it.

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: I... still haven't delivered the killing blow.

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: You can still say goodbye, if you want.

steps.name: Juana
steps.text: Gracias.
The Seaborn writhes, its appendages twitching as swords scrape dully against one another.
But this sound soon fades, along with the Seaborn's feeble breathing. Juana knows that the last vestige of its life is slipping away.
With its last bit of strength, it lifts itself from the ground, using the swords impaling it as support.

steps.name: Juana
steps.text: I'm sorry for imprisoning you in this cave for so long.

steps.name: Juana
steps.text: Your suffering will end soon.

steps.name: Juana
steps.text: I'm glad I met that boy, so you could meet your end by the sword in an honorable duel.

steps.name: Juana
steps.text: Rather than being put down as a monster...

steps.name: Juana
steps.text: So many have failed... but he succeeded.

steps.name: Juana
steps.text: If he's willing to go out to sea with us, surely he would be your equal as captain.
Juana approaches the creature, places a hand upon its smooth face, and gazes into its clouded eyes.
It struggles as it senses her approach, but its once-strong appendages betray it, and it falls to the ground.
Juana holds its head and places it upon her knees.
The light-emitting organ on its forehead dims. Juana is reminded of that night many years ago, when she saw a tiny sailboat from beneath the surface.
On that boat stood a young man, gazing curiously into the water, lamp in hand.

steps.name: Juana
steps.text: May your soul be freed from the Salt Flat, and return to the ocean with the clouds and rain.

steps.name: Juana
steps.text: May we meet again on the boundless ocean.

steps.name: Juana
steps.text: Farewell, my love.
Juana feels a stinging pain in her chest. This is good. It is a sign that she still lives, and has not been numbed over the past century.
Deep in the ocean, in an Ægir city, the years pass like a single day.
Deep in the Salt Flat, in an Iberian settlement, life is bland as water.
It is only upon the waves, in strife and struggle, that her blood flows, that her heart beats.
It is only then that she feels hunger, the desire to take a bite out of tomorrow, and cough violently at its taste.
She will bite out the shape of the future, one mouthful at a time, and down it with bitter brine.

steps.name: Pascuala
steps.text: Let go of me, you piece of finshit!

steps.name: Pascuala
steps.text: Juana and Isidro will have you all killed when they see what you're doing to me!

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: Shut her up.

steps.name: Pascuala
steps.text: Finshit... mmph, nnf!

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: I've sent out word, Rus. The escort will be ready soon. You leave with the chica.

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: I'll look for the compass in the boss's room and catch up once I find it.

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: Er, I'm not quite sure I understand what's going on here. Is this a mutiny?

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: Could somebody explain things to me?

steps.name: Rus
steps.text: Do we hand him over too?

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: Aye.

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: Thorns won't...

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: I... mmph, nnf!

steps.name: Rus
steps.text: Finally, some peace and quiet.

steps.name: Pascuala
steps.text: Mmpf...

steps.name: Nene
steps.text: (Pokes head out from under the table)

steps.name: Pascuala
steps.text: (C'mon... over here...)
She tries to signal it with her eyes, but Rus and Javier's footsteps send it back into hiding.
She grits her teeth and opens her eyes wide, trying to put on the fiercest look she can muster to scare it into coming out.

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: What? Salt got in your eyes?

steps.name: Pascuala
steps.text: Hmm?

steps.name: Rus
steps.text: Just leave her be.

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: Wish I could, but the way she's scrunching her face is an eyesore.

steps.name: Pascuala
steps.text: Mmph?!

steps.name: Pascuala
steps.text: Mmph—!!

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: Hmph, nothing...

steps.name: Rus
steps.text: Lemme take a look.
As Rus approaches, Pascuala struggles even harder against her fetters.
That is, until she catches a glimpse of Elysium slowly edging towards the table, and the saltfin beneath.
She stops struggling and keeps her gaze firmly on the duo in front of her, doing her utmost not to avert her eyes even a little bit.

steps.name: Juana
steps.text: Nene? What are you doing here?

steps.name: Nene
steps.text: Mmph!

steps.name: Juana
steps.text: What's this on your fin?

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: That's... Elysium's flag. Something must have happened back at the fleet.

steps.name: Juana
steps.text: Let's hurry!
